links.note: Was on 32838 The Five Oceans Named. Drawing the continents freehand without looking at the maps and then comparing with the chapter's map is verbatim one of the closing questions listed in 32846.
Was on 32845 World Oceans Day. Labelling all the continents and oceans on an outline map is verbatim one of the closing questions in 32846, and the crossword that follows it is there too.

Was on 32836 Landmass, Continent, and Varuna. The crossword clue describes a landmass that is not a continent and is surrounded by sea, which is the island, defined in 32843 - surrounded by water on all sides, and distinguished from a continent only by size.
Was on 32843 What Makes an Island. The blue planet seen from space, and blue standing for water, are 32835's opening observation.
Was on 32845 World Oceans Day, the chapter's closing section. The claim that both oceans and continents play a vital role in shaping the climate of the Earth is stated in 32836.
Was on 32835 Three-Fourths Water. The Indian Navy's motto Sam No Varunah, invoking the Vedic deity Varuna, is in 32836's DON'T MISS OUT box.
Was on 32843 What Makes an Island. That seawater is salty and unfit for consumption by most land animals including humans is stated in 32837.

Was on 32835 Three-Fourths Water. The question is verbatim 32837's THINK ABOUT IT - if there is such abundance of water on the planet, why is there so much talk of water scarcity - and its answer is that the seawater is salty and freshwater a very small proportion.
Was on 32845 World Oceans Day. The five oceans - Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic and Southern - are named in 32838.
Was on 32838 The Five Oceans Named, which lists them without ranking them. The order of size, with the Pacific largest, is given in 32839.
Was on 32838 The Five Oceans Named. That the Arctic is the smallest of the five is part of the size order given in 32839.

Was on 32843 What Makes an Island, which defines islands in general. India's two island groups and their waters - Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal, Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea - are named in 32844.

Was on 32838 The Five Oceans Named. The Olympic rings representing five inhabited continents - Africa, America, Asia, Australia and Europe - are in 32842's DON'T MISS OUT box, where they appear as a fifth way of counting.
Was on 32835 Three-Fourths Water. Islands defined as the smaller pieces of land the continents leave out, surrounded by water on all sides, are 32843's subject.
Was on 32838 The Five Oceans Named. That the oceans have smaller extensions with various names such as sea, bay and gulf is stated in 32837.
Was on 32845 World Oceans Day. That oceans and continents are not distributed equally between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres opens 32837.

Was on 32837 Salty Ocean, Scarce Fresh Water, which names sea, bay and gulf as a class. That the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal are the two parts of the Indian Ocean on either side of India is stated in 32839.
